I need to think this through as myself — a 63-year-old man who's been working this land since I was 18. I've got 7 mu in the southern part of Quzhou, just me and my wife at home now. Our son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang and sends some money back, but not much. I can't afford to get this wrong.

**Cotton again this year.** I've been growing cotton on this land for more than 20 years. I thought about switching to wheat-maize like some folks, but that double cropping is too much labor for an old man and a woman. Cotton gives one big harvest, and I know it. The soil here is decent — a bit sandy, but it's always grown cotton fine. I'll plant all 7 mu to cotton. No point in dividing up such a small plot.

**Planting time.** I'll start sowing around April 20th, after the Qingming festival when the soil warms up. Last year I planted a bit early and some seeds rotted in a cold snap. I'll wait until I'm sure this time. If the weather looks good, maybe April 18th. Harvest will be September through October, picking in three or four rounds. That's just how cotton is.

**Seed.** I buy improved hybrid seed from the county supply store every year — I don't save my own, the hybrid vigor drops off. It's about 50 yuan per mu for the seed. The extension people keep talking about some new Bt varieties, and my neighbor Zhang tried one last year and got good yield with less spraying for bollworm. I might try that — the seed costs a bit more, maybe 55 yuan, but if I spray less, it could save money.

**Fertilizer.** The extension guy said I should put down compound fertilizer with about 12 kg nitrogen per mu, split between base and topdressing. I usually do a bit more than that — last year I put about 15 kg N equivalent per mu and got around 280 kg of lint. I'll do the same this year. Base fertilizer: about 25 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu at planting, which gives me about 3.75 kg N, plus some P and K. Then topdress with urea twice — once at flowering in July, about 10 kg urea per mu (that's about 4.6 kg N), and once in early August when the bolls are setting, another 8 kg urea (about 3.7 kg N). Total N comes to about 12 kg per mu. I know the extension says I could go higher, but fertilizer prices went up and I've only got so much cash. 12 kg has worked fine for me.

**Irrigation.** I've got a tube well, but the electricity for pumping keeps getting more expensive. Cotton doesn't need as much water as wheat, thank heavens. I'll irrigate twice: once at flowering in mid-July if it doesn't rain, and once in August when the bolls are filling. Maybe a third time if it's very dry, but twice is usually enough. Each irrigation costs me about 40 yuan in electricity for the 7 mu.

**Pesticide.** Cotton needs spraying, no way around it. I'll use a pre-emergent herbicide right after planting to keep the weeds down — hand-weeding 7 mu is too much for us now. Then for insects, I'll spray insecticide 3 or 4 times during the season. If I get the Bt seed, maybe only 2 or 3 times for bollworm instead of 4. I'll also need a fungicide spray once if it gets too humid in summer.

**Tillage.** I'll plow the field once in early April with my small tractor, then harrow it fine before planting. Nothing fancy. The tractor's old but it works.

**Labor.** Planting and managing the field is me and my wife — maybe 15 family days total through the season. For picking, cotton is a killer. Each mu needs about 8-10 days of picking labor if you do it by hand. Last year we hired two women from the village to help with the first big picking in late September. I'll probably do the same this year — hire about 10 days of labor at 100 yuan per day. My wife and I can handle the rest, but our backs aren't what they used to be.

**Yield.** Last year I got about 280 kg per mu. The year before was better, around 310. I think this year if the weather cooperates, I'll get about 270-280 kg per mu. I'm not expecting a bumper year — I'm old enough to know you don't get those every season. I'm hoping for 280.

**Money.** The seed, fertilizer, pesticides, irrigation electricity, and hired picking labor will run me about 2,100 to 2,300 yuan for the 7 mu. That's a lot of money for us. I have to keep some cash aside — my wife needs her blood pressure medicine, and you never know what breaks on the tractor. But if I cut too much on fertilizer or spray, I might lose half the crop. Better to spend what I need and tighten our belts on other things.
